text:
sara-support: Hey team — customer `acme-inc` reporting intermittent 502s from hosted API when uploading long streaming prompts for embeddings. Happens ~every 30–90s during a burst. Seeing: 

sara-support: curl reproduction they sent: 
```
curl -X POST 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  --data '{"input": "<very long prompt repeated>"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings 
```

sara-support: Root log snippet (edge): 
```
[2024-11-11T18:34:22Z] upstream_write stalled 12000ms conn=10.2.3.4:45123 -> 172.31.5.7:8080 tid=abcd1234
[2024-11-11T18:34:22Z] envoy: downstream reset by peer, code=502, trace=trace-acme-0001
```

sara-support: customer says it only fails when they send one big JSON body (not chunked). They tried retrying and got success on 2nd attempt.

jon-eng-sre: Thanks — can you paste the trace id and any ingress headers (x-request-id / x-forwarded-for)? Also which region (us-east-1)?

sara-support: trace=trace-acme-0001, x-request-id=acme-req-9923, region=us-east-1. Attached small raw HTTP headers: 
```
:method: POST
:path: /v1/embeddings
content-length: 1245678
content-type: application/json
user-agent: acme-sdk/1.2.3
```

mike-runtime: This looks like an upstream socket stall on large payloads — likely the write buffer fills and upstream can't accept, then envoy closes with 502. Two suspects: http2 flow control windowing + proxy_buffer config on the nginx frontdoor. Are these requests hitting frontdoor or midproxy?

lisa-oncall: Frontdoor (nginx) in eu->us egress for that tenant is routing via midproxy pool A. We had a small config tweak 12h ago that changed `proxy_buffer_size` on the frontdoor to 8k for perf tests.

mike-runtime: Bingo. If `proxy_buffer_size` is too small and client sends a single large body, nginx will chunk into temporary files or stall upstream writes. Envoy then sees stalled downstream and surfaces 502. We should repro locally with a single large non-chunked POST.

sara-support: I can repro with a curl one-liner: 
```
python -c "print('a'*1000000)" > big.json
curl -v -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary @big.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
```

jon-eng-sre: Nice. For immediate mitigation: 1) increase `proxy_buffer_size` to 32k on frontdoor for affected pool, 2) enable chunked transfer encoding on the SDK side (work with Acme), 3) add an envoy retry for 502 on idempotent upload endpoints? Note: uploads aren't idempotent.

lisa-oncall: I pushed a quick bump to `proxy_buffer_size=32k` on pool A and rolled to 3 nodes (deploy id: fd-roll-20241111-9). Monitoring now.

edge-bot: [alert] 2024-11-11T18:46:05Z - elevated 502 rate in us-east-1 frontdoor pool A (10m avg -> 3.2% -> rollback recommended)

mike-runtime: Watch the queue length and `upstream_write_time` histograms. If stalled writes persist after buffer bump, we should also tune http2 max frame size and h2 flow window.

jon-eng-sre: Can you attach sample tcpdump from frontdoor->midproxy when it fails? Need to confirm whether ACKs stop (client stalls) or midproxy stops reading.

sara-support: Uploaded tcpdump snippet to the thread: /mnt/support/artifacts/acme/tcpdump-1707772468.pcap (internal link). Observed long write stalls followed by RST from midproxy.

mike-runtime: RST from midproxy suggests upstream backlog or thread pool saturation reading large bodies. Next step: check midproxy worker queue metrics and increase `proxy_read_timeout` or worker count for that pool.

lisa-oncall: Midproxy pool A worker count was at 4 per host during the incident; bumped to 8 and restarted service (mp-poolA-scale-20241111). We'll keep watchers on CPU.

sara-support: Customer confirmed immediate improvement — success rate back to normal after buffer + worker bump. They also agreed to try chunked uploads in their SDK.

jon-eng-sre: Action items: 
- sara-support: coordinate with Acme SDK team to roll chunked transfer recommendation and sample code.
- mike-runtime: run a load test with 1MB non-chunked bodies against frontdoor+midproxy (simulate pool A) and capture metrics.
- lisa-oncall: keep the frontdoor buffer bump and midproxy worker scale for 24h, then we can plan a controlled config revert if stable.

mike-runtime: Long-term: add a telemetry alert for upstream_write_time > 5s and automatic progressive increase of `proxy_buffer_size` for tenants with large payload patterns.

sara-support: Noted — I'll update the ticket and follow up with customer tomorrow. Thanks all :thumbsup:
